text:
maria: Quick q — for active/active tenants that have an EU residency flag, how fine-grained should our fallback policy be? Region-level fallback keeps data in-region but higher latency during failover. Zone-level (AZ) fallback is lower latency but risks crossing legal boundary if AZ spans jurisdictions. Thoughts?
kevin: +1 this is the crux. my gut: default to region-level for residency=true, but allow opt-in for lower-latency AZ fallback via tenant config.
olga: Agree with region-by-default. Also we need to surface the risk in the console and API (explicit flag). Don't silently cross boundaries.
maria: Yeah — we should also think about cold-cache penalty. region-only fallback means full KV rehydrate which can spike p50/p95. We need cost/latency tradeoff documented.
lia: Could we do a hybrid: prefer AZ fallback within same legal region, but disallow if the AZ's network path will egress to a different country? i.e., check data-plane pathing before allowing.
kevin: That gets tricky to maintain. We already have a routing matrix that annotates region->country. Maybe simpler: annotate AZs with country code and only allow AZ fallback if AZ.country == tenant.country.
olga: That would work for most clouds. Edge-case: some cloud providers expose AZs that straddle internal boundaries. We should default to conservative if AZ.country is unknown.
maria: Operationally, what should the API look like? Proposal: tenant config object gets residency: { "required": "eu", "fallback_granularity": "region|az|preference" } — default fallback_granularity = region for required residency.
kevin: +1 to schema. Also add: fallback_granularity: preference means we try az but fall back to region if legal check fails at runtime.
lia: runtime legal check: who owns that service? Is this on the control plane or per-proxy? We should avoid adding expensive network checks per-request.
maria: Good point. Maybe compile a legal-allowlist at deploy-time and push to edge proxies as rules. update cadence: on infra changes or tenant settings change.
kevin: We should also add telemetry metric: fallback.privacy_violation_attempts and fallback.used_granularity so we can measure how often AZ vs region gets used and if we ever attempted to cross boundary and were blocked.
olga: +1. And alert on any "blocked cross-boundary attempt" for enterprise compliance teams.
lia: Also need a playbook for disaster mode: if the entire region is down and tenant.requires_residency=true, do we block traffic completely or provide an explicit override in support panel? For some customers they prefer availability over strict residency in catastrophic events.
maria: My proposal: block by default. Provide a time-limited override (3hr) that requires signed acceptance in console + audit log. That fits compliance needs.
kevin: And log the override as a tenant-level event, with signer, reason. Exportable to SIEM.
maria: small implementation notes: 1) Extend residency table to include AZ.country and AZ.legal_id (string) 2) routing policy evaluation order: prefer tenant.route_hint -> preference -> az (if allowed) -> region 3) telemetry hooks for each decision.
lia: And include a small config example for API users in the console:

maria (code): ```json
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "residency": {
    "required": "EU",
    "fallback_granularity": "preference"
  }
}
```

kevin: Nice. Ops question: who will own rollout of the rules to proxies? eng-infra or eng-runtime?
olga: eng-runtime should own the evaluation logic; eng-infra owns the distribution pipeline for the rule bundles. We'll coordinate.
maria: Ok next steps: i'll draft a short RFC with the API shape, default policy, and the override workflow. kevin/olga/lia — can you review the RFC when i post it? aim to have it in 72h.
kevin: I will review.
lia: I'll take the section on runtime checks and distribution.
olga: I'll add compliance notes and telemetry requirements.
deploy-bot: note: created follow-up task INF-8246 "residency fallback RFC" assigned to maria, kevin, olga, lia, due 3 days. :white_check_mark:
